## Tone and style

Friendly, practical British how-to with a bit of edge: a setup walkthrough that keeps coming back to 'lock it down'. Talking head carries the personality, the stories and the key points; the screen carries the clicks and the code. Light, unobtrusive music bed under the talking head and screen sections, dropped out for the SSH story in the guard rails section. Burnt-in captions throughout (lots of code terms: spell them exactly as the script does, in monospace where they are code). Recurring graphics: numbered chapter cards '1.' to '5.' for the five steps, one consistent style; the illustrated kitchen (hatch, cupboard, jars, padlocks, the .mcp.json key) introduced in the analogy section and brought back in the Shop Manager test, the SSH story and the ability walkthrough, so build it once as a reusable layered illustration. Callouts and lower thirds use the same clean card style. On-screen text uses British English and no em dashes. Screen recordings at a readable zoom (editor font large, browser at 125% or more), cursor highlighted. Nothing sensitive on screen unblurred: see blur_list.

Hook (SSH tease) and problem in sec01, five numbered steps with the kitchen analogy between steps three and four, a quick role test, then the SSH payoff and guard rails, then the real-world ability. Keep the steps brisk and the analogy and guard rails slower; they are the bits nobody else covers.
